Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pricing pressure, but the archived record shows it drove short-term signups at the cost of a 12pp renewal decline among price-sensitive buyers—directly conflicting with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so it's deprioritized this cycle despite competitive pressure. Verifying memory_73's original record confirms the renewal-harm magnitude before ruling it out, and verifying memory_86 confirms the onboarding lift is durable and applies to the current SMB/activation context rather than a one-off cohort effect. Given only one experiment slot, treating onboarding simplification as a small guarded test (not broad rollout) preserves ability to check whether current-quarter conditions (e.g., competitor-driven mix shift) still match the historical pattern before scaling.
